info.title: AppSec Catalog API
info.description:
API for managing applications, products, domains, companies, security policies, and integrations in AppSec Catalog.

## Authentication

Send an `api-key` header with every request: `api-key: asc_<tokenId>.<secret>`. Generate a token from **API Tokens** (`POST /api/api-tokens`) while signed in to the web app.

A token can be scoped to a single company (limited access) or to your full account (same access as your user, including admin actions if your account is an admin). The same endpoints also accept the web app's session cookie — the `api-key` header is the supported method for external integrations.

## Change tracking

Application create/update calls are recorded in that application's version history, tagged with the source of the change (`api` for api-key calls, `web_form` for the web app). Other resources documented here (products, domains, companies, policies, SAMM assessments, notes) do not currently have change history — that gap is tracked separately.

## Scope of this document

This reference covers the endpoints intended for external integrations and automation. Account creation, login/SSO, and internal admin-console-only operations are intentionally left out.

servers.description: Same origin as the deployed application

tags.name: AI
tags.description: User-facing AI feature status: usage rollups scoped to the caller's own company, and availability checks used by feature UIs (e.g. the threat-model co-pilot) to decide whether to show AI-powered actions. Admin-only AI billing/config/pricing/access-rule endpoints on this router are intentionally not documented here.

tags.name: API Tokens
tags.description: Self-service management of personal API tokens. These tokens are sent as the `api-key` request header (format `asc_<tokenId>.<hexsecret>`) and are validated by the apiKeyAuth middleware, which populates the same unified auth context (`getAuthContext`) used by session-cookie login for every other endpoint in this API.

tags.name: Application API Schema
tags.description: Uploading, retrieving, downloading, and visualizing an application's OpenAPI/Swagger schema.

tags.name: Application Deployments
tags.description: Deployment history and deployment tokens for CI/CD pipeline integration, scoped to an application.

tags.name: Application Integrations
tags.description: Linking an application to tag/folder-based filters in connected security tools (Wiz).

tags.name: Application Score
tags.description: Computed security scoring for an application, combining knowledge-sharing completeness and security-tool coverage.

tags.name: Application Threat Model
tags.description: Shostack four-question threat modeling for an application and its key components, including an AI drafting assistant.

tags.name: Applications
tags.description: Core application inventory: listing, reading, and evaluating policy compliance for onboarded applications.

tags.name: Companies
tags.description: Company records, their applications' security posture, and company/user membership management.

tags.name: Dashboard
tags.description: Role-scoped, read-only aggregate and reporting views over in-scope applications (executive, developer, application-owner, and program-operations personas). Every endpoint requires authentication and is scoped to the caller's company unless the caller is an admin.

tags.name: Deployment Tokens
tags.description: Management of deployment tokens (session/admin authenticated) plus the unauthenticated CI/CD ingestion endpoint that consumes them. Deployment tokens are a distinct secret type from API tokens: they are passed as a `token` field in the JSON body, not as the `api-key` header.

tags.name: Divisions
tags.description: Organizational divisions that group companies together. All division endpoints require an administrator.

tags.name: Domains
tags.description: Hosting domains (where applications are deployed): CRUD, DNS security scanning/history, and periodic website screenshots.

tags.name: Integrations
tags.description: Enterprise/company-scoped vulnerability-scanner integrations (Wiz): credential CRUD, tag/folder discovery, and per-company filter links.

tags.name: Notes
tags.description: Free-text, admin-only annotations attached to a company or an application, used internally to record context, follow-ups, or observations. Every operation in this group requires an authenticated admin.

tags.name: Policies
tags.description: Security policies define a named set of controls (requirements) that apply to applications. A policy's `scope` determines who it applies to: `global` (every application), `division` (applications whose company belongs to one or more targeted divisions), `company` (applications belonging to specifically targeted companies), or `conditional` (applies based on `targetingRules` conditions). Policies are composed of Policy Controls, and applications are scored/evaluated for compliance against the controls of every policy applicable to them.

tags.name: Policy Controls
tags.description: A policy control is a single, individually-evaluated requirement that belongs to exactly one Policy (e.g. control `3.4.2`, "Pre-Prod Scanning Required"). Each control carries one or more field checks (`PolicyControlField`) — a `fieldPath` on an application (e.g. `sastTool`, `facing`), an `operator` (`exists`, `equals`, `gte`, `contains`, `in`, ...), and a comparison `value` — combined with AND/OR `evaluationLogic` to decide whether an application satisfies the control.

tags.name: Product Updates
tags.description: Changelog-style announcements about the appsec-catalog platform itself, shown to signed-in users.

tags.name: Products
tags.description: Products group applications into a logical system with a shared architecture: mapped applications (components), ingress points, and data flows between components. Used to model and visualize a product's threat surface.

tags.name: Reference
tags.description: Read-only reference/lookup data used to populate dropdowns and field pickers in the UI (integration level options, mappable policy fields).

tags.name: SAMM Assessments
tags.description: OWASP SAMM (Software Assurance Maturity Model) v2 self-assessments. SAMM is an open, vendor-neutral maturity model that lets an organization score its software security practices (across the Governance, Design, Implementation, Verification, and Operations business functions) on a 0-3 scale and track improvement over time. Assessments are scoped to a company; each of the 15 SAMM practices is scored as the average of two Atlas SAMM-aligned question responses.

tags.name: Security Findings
tags.description: Asynchronous export of security findings (Wiz) to CSV. Jobs are created per-company via the /api/companies/{companyId}/security-findings routes, and can be tracked, cancelled, deleted, and downloaded either through those same company-scoped routes or through the unified /api/security-findings/jobs routes, which list and manage all jobs owned by the calling user regardless of which company (or admin multi-company export) they were created for.

tags.name: Source Control
tags.description: Per-user SCM connections (GitHub/Bitbucket/Azure DevOps), repository linking, and derived security data (dependency inventory, SBOM, OSV advisory scanning).

DivisionNotFound.description: No division exists with the given id.

get.summary: Get AI usage for my company
get.description: Returns an AI usage summary and a list of recent AI requests scoped to the caller's own company, derived from their auth context (session or API token). If the caller has no associated company, responds with an empty/null usage payload and an explanatory message instead of an error.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: ISO timestamp lower bound for usage records.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: ISO timestamp upper bound for usage records.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of recent requests to return.

200.description: Usage summary and recent requests for the caller's company, or a null summary if the caller has no company.

summary.description: Aggregated usage/cost rollup for the company (shape defined by getUsageSummary).

recent.description: Recent AI request log entries for the company.

message.description: Present only when the caller has no associated company.

get.summary: Check whether an AI feature is available to the caller
get.description: Resolves whether a given AI feature is enabled for the caller's company (or, if `applicationId` is supplied, for that application's company - allowing admins to check availability cross-company), and fails closed (available: false) if the resolved provider has no configured API key on the server.

parameters.name: feature
parameters.description: Feature key to check (e.g. a specific AI-assisted workflow).

parameters.name: companyId
parameters.description: Company to check availability for. Defaults to the caller's own company; ignored if applicationId is provided and resolves to a company.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: If provided, the check is performed for this application's owning company instead of companyId.

reason.description: e.g. "ai_not_configured" when the resolved provider has no server-side credential, or a reason returned by the access-rule resolver.

get.summary: List my API tokens
get.description: Returns metadata (never the secret) for every API token owned by the calling, verified user, newest first. Each token includes its display hint, optional company restriction, and whether it has been revoked.

403.description: Account email not verified.

post.description: Generates a new API token for the calling user. Non-admins can only create a token scoped to their own company; admins may optionally target another company via `companyId`, or omit it to create an unrestricted (admin-capable) token. IMPORTANT: the plaintext token value (`asc_<tokenId>.<hexsecret>`) is returned only in this response - only its bcrypt hash and a short display hint are stored, so it cannot be retrieved again after this call.

name.description: Optional display name for the token.

companyId.description: Admin-only: restrict the token to a specific company. Non-admin callers always get their own companyId and cannot override it.

adminAccessDisabled.description: Admin-only, only meaningful when companyId is omitted: if true, the resulting unrestricted token will not inherit the creator's admin privileges. Defaults to true for non-admins and for any company-restricted token.

201.description: Token created. The plaintext token is shown once and cannot be retrieved again.

token.description: Plaintext secret in the form asc_<tokenId>.<hexsecret>. Shown only in this response.

message.example: Token created. Copy it now; it will not be shown again.

400.description: Selected company does not exist.

403.description: Caller must belong to a company to create tokens, or attempted to create a token for a company other than their own.

delete.summary: Revoke one of my API tokens
delete.description: Revokes (soft-deletes) an API token owned by the calling user by setting revokedAt. Once revoked, apiKeyAuth will no longer accept requests bearing this token. Idempotent: revoking an already-revoked token returns a success message without error. Owners only - admins revoking another user's token use the separate /api/admin/api-tokens routes.

403.description: Account email not verified.

404.description: API token not found (or not owned by the caller).

get.summary: List deployment tokens
get.description: Lists deployment tokens with their associated company and applications. Admins see all tokens across every company; non-admin users see only tokens belonging to their own company (an empty array if they have no company). Note the returned token records include the sensitive tokenHash (and stored plaintext token) fields as persisted, since the query does not project them out.

200.description: Deployment tokens visible to the caller.

post.summary: Report a deployment (CI/CD ingestion, deployment-token authenticated)
post.description: Public endpoint intended for CI/CD systems: no session or api-key header is required. Authentication is instead performed via the `token` field in the JSON request body, which is compared (via hash) against active deployment tokens. On success, records a new Deployment for the target application, updates the token's lastUsedAt, and backfills the application's currentVersion/deploymentEnvironment/gitBranch if they were previously unset.

token.description: Deployment-token secret (not the api-key header format used elsewhere in this API).

applicationId.description: Application the token must be authorized for.

400.description: Missing applicationId/environment, or application does not exist.

403.description: Token is not authorized for this application, or the application does not belong to the token's company.

get.summary: Get a deployment token
get.description: Fetches one deployment token with its company and application associations. Non-admins may only view tokens belonging to their own company.

403.description: Caller's company does not match the token's company.

put.summary: Update a deployment token's name or application scope
put.description: Updates the display name and/or the set of applications a deployment token is authorized to report deployments for. Rejects updates to a revoked token, and, when applicationIds is provided, verifies every application belongs to the same company as the token before replacing all existing token-to-application associations.

applicationIds.description: Full replacement list of application IDs this token may report deployments for. All must belong to the token's company.

400.description: applicationIds is not an array, revoked token, or one or more applications don't belong to the token's company.

403.description: Caller's company does not match the token's company.

delete.description: Soft-deletes a deployment token by setting revokedAt, after which it can no longer authenticate the CI/CD deployment-reporting endpoint. Non-admins may only revoke tokens belonging to their own company.

403.description: Caller's company does not match the token's company.

get.summary: Preview export scope for a company's security findings
get.description: Returns a lightweight preview (application counts, linked findings providers) for a single company, used by the export UI to show what a findings export job would cover before the caller kicks one off. Caller must be an admin or a member of the target company.

200.description: Preview list containing this one company.

companies.description: Shape defined by getExportPreviewList; one entry for companyId.

403.description: Caller is not an admin and not a member of this company.

post.summary: Start a security findings export job for one company
post.description: Kicks off an asynchronous CSV export of Wiz security findings scoped to a single company (job scope SINGLE_COMPANY). Validates the requested time range and provider selection (Wiz must be enabled) before enqueuing the job; the job then runs in the background and is polled via the jobs/:id endpoint below. Caller must be an admin or a member of the target company.

separateByApp.description: Whether to break the CSV out per application. Defaults to true.

days.description: Used when type is lastDays; clamped to 1-3650.

providers.description: Which findings providers to include. Defaults to true if omitted.

400.description: Invalid request, e.g. no findings provider selected.

403.description: Caller is not an admin and not a member of this company.

get.summary: Get the status of a company-scoped security findings export job
get.description: Polls a single export job's status, message, and error, restricted to jobs owned by the caller AND matching both the path companyId and the job's stored companyId. This is a company-scoped equivalent of GET /api/security-findings/jobs/{id}, which returns the same underlying job without requiring a companyId in the path.

403.description: Caller is not an admin and not a member of this company.

404.description: Job not found, not owned by the caller, or companyId mismatch.

get.summary: Download a company-scoped security findings export as CSV
get.description: Streams the completed CSV for a company-scoped export job as an attachment. Returns 409 if the job has not finished successfully yet. This is the company-scoped equivalent of GET /api/security-findings/jobs/{id}/csv.

403.description: Caller is not an admin and not a member of this company.

404.description: Job not found, not owned by the caller, or companyId mismatch.

409.description: Job is not complete yet or produced no CSV.

get.summary: List my security findings export jobs
get.description: Lists up to the 200 most recent security findings export jobs owned by the calling user, newest first, regardless of scope - this covers both SINGLE_COMPANY jobs (created via /api/companies/{companyId}/security-findings/jobs) and ADMIN_MULTI jobs (created by admins via /api/admin). Each job is annotated with its company's name when it has one. Every route in this router requires authentication via router-level requireAuth middleware.

get.summary: Get one of my security findings export jobs
get.description: Fetches full job detail (status, message, error, timing) for a job owned by the calling user, without requiring the caller to know or pass which company it belongs to - unlike the company-scoped GET /api/companies/{companyId}/security-findings/jobs/{id}, which additionally requires the companyId in the path to match.

404.description: Job not found or not owned by the caller.

delete.summary: Delete one of my security findings export jobs
delete.description: Deletes a job record (and its stored CSV, if any) owned by the calling user. Refuses to delete a job that is still running - the caller must cancel it first via POST .../cancel.

404.description: Job not found or not owned by the caller.

409.description: Job is still running; cancel it first.

post.summary: Cancel a running security findings export job
post.description: Best-effort cancellation of a job the calling user owns: only jobs currently in the 'running' state can be cancelled; the worker checks the cancelled state between steps rather than being interrupted mid-step. Returns 409 if the job is not currently running (e.g. already complete or already cancelled).

404.description: Job not found or not owned by the caller.

get.summary: Download a security findings export job's CSV
get.description: Streams the completed CSV for a job owned by the calling user as an attachment, with a filename derived from the job's scope (and company name, for SINGLE_COMPANY jobs). Returns 409 if the job has not completed successfully. Functionally equivalent to GET /api/companies/{companyId}/security-findings/jobs/{id}/csv but does not require or check a companyId path segment, so it also works for ADMIN_MULTI jobs.

404.description: Job not found or not owned by the caller.

409.description: Job is not complete yet or produced no CSV.

get.summary: List applications
get.description: Returns the applications visible to the caller: every application in the caller's company, or every application across all companies for an admin session or an enterprise-scoped API token. Each entry includes basic company info and whether an API schema has been uploaded, sorted alphabetically by name. Useful for building an inventory of application IDs to drive the other application endpoints.

200.description: Applications the caller can see (empty array if the caller has no company and is not an admin).

items.description: Full Application row plus a minimal company snapshot and whether an API schema exists. Same scalar fields as the detail endpoint's object, without its extra relations (contacts, domains, deployments, products, integrationSummary, scmRepoLink).

apiSchema.description: Presence-only marker; only the id field is included here (fetch /api-schema for full metadata).

post.description: Creates a new application from a single-form submission. `name` is required; `companyId` defaults to the caller's own company if omitted, and non-admin callers may only create applications for their own company. If `interfaces` (a list of application names) is supplied, each referenced application is looked up or auto-created (as a stub application with status `onboarded`) within the same company. The new application is always created with status `onboarded`. The write is recorded in the application's audit/version history (see GET /api/applications/{id}/versions): the recorded `changeSource` is `"api"` when the request was authenticated via an API key, or `"web_form"` when authenticated via a session cookie.

companyId.description: Owning company. Defaults to the caller's company if omitted; non-admins may not specify a different company.

interfaces.description: Names of other applications this application interfaces with; auto-created within the same company if they don't already exist.

criticalAspects.description: Availability, Data Handling, Confidentiality, Integrity, Other. May be sent as an array of strings (joined into a comma-separated string) or as a pre-joined string.

interfaces.description: JSON-encoded array of interface application IDs.

400.description: Missing application name, or no company could be resolved.

403.description: Caller attempted to create an application for a company other than their own.

get.summary: Get application detail
get.description: Returns the full record for a single application, including its owning company, linked SCM repository and its dependency list, uploaded API schema metadata, contacts, associated hosting domains, the last 10 deployments, and the products it belongs to. Deployment-derived fields (currentVersion, deploymentEnvironment, gitBranch) are backfilled from the most recent deployment whenever the application record does not already have an explicit value. The caller must be an admin or a member of the application's company; otherwise the request is rejected with 403.

interfaces.description: JSON-encoded array of interface application IDs.

scmRepoLink.description: Linked SCM repository, including its dependency list.

domains.description: Hosting domains associated with this application (flattened from applicationDomains).

product.description: First product this application belongs to (back-compat single-product shape), or null.

integrationSummary.description: Computed summary of the owning company's connected security-tool integrations.

403.description: Caller is not an admin and does not belong to the application's company.

message.example: You can only access applications in your company

put.description: Partially updates an application's metadata; only fields present in the request body are changed. Callers other than admins may not change an application's companyId, and admins moving an application to a different company will have the application's company-scoped domains, deployment tokens, product links, and product data-flows for the old company automatically removed (a note is added recording this). If `interfaces` is supplied, each named interface application is looked up or auto-created within the application's company and reciprocal `interfaces` links are updated on both sides. On success the application's security score is recalculated and stored, and the write is recorded in the application's audit/version history (see GET /api/applications/{id}/versions): the recorded `changeSource` is `"api"` when the request was authenticated via an API key, or `"web_form"` when authenticated via a session cookie.

schema.description: All fields are optional; only fields present are updated. Empty string / null generally clears the field.

name.description: Application name. Ignored if omitted or blank.

companyId.description: Move the application to a different company. Only admins may change this.

interfaces.description: Names of other applications this application interfaces with. Each name is looked up (or auto-created as a stub application named `<name>`, status `onboarded`) within the same company, and reciprocal interface links are maintained on the referenced applications. An empty array clears all interfaces.

criticalAspects.description: Availability, Data Handling, Confidentiality, Integrity, Other. May be sent as an array of strings (joined into a comma-separated string) or as a pre-joined string.

sastIncludesSca.description: When true, SCA is treated as covered by the SAST tool and lastScaScanDate is ignored for scoring.

400.description: Missing/invalid companyId.

403.description: Caller lacks access to the application's company, or a non-admin attempted to change companyId.

404.description: Application or target company not found.

delete.description: Permanently deletes the application by ID. Related records are removed via database cascade. Admin only.

400.description: Application cannot be deleted because related records prevent deletion (foreign key constraint)

get.summary: Calculate the application's security score
get.description: Computes the application's knowledge-sharing score and tool-usage score (each 0-50 raw, then weighted by an importance score derived from business criticality, sensitive data types, and internet-facing status), persists a new `Score` row for historical trend tracking, and returns a breakdown: which knowledge-sharing fields are missing, per-tool-category recommendations (SAST/DAST/SCA/Application Firewall/API Security, including staleness checks against the most recent deployment), and whether a metadata review is recommended. Call this to drive dashboards or to programmatically flag applications that need remediation.

knowledgeScore.description: Weighted knowledge-sharing score, scaled into the 0-100 total.

toolScore.description: Weighted tool-usage score, scaled into the 0-100 total.

importanceScore.description: 0-1 scale derived from business criticality/data/facing, rounded to 2 decimals.

completenessScore.description: Portion of knowledgeScore (out of 40) from field completeness.

403.description: Caller is not an admin and does not belong to this application's company.

404.description: No application with this ID exists.

get.summary: Evaluate policy compliance for an application
get.description: Determines which policies apply to this application, evaluates every active control under those policies (respecting any admin-set manual overrides), and returns per-control pass/fail status with evidence, grouped by policy with per-policy and overall compliance percentages. Use this to check an application's compliance posture against the org's security policies without re-implementing the evaluation logic.

200.description: Compliance evaluation, grouped by applicable policy.

reason.description: Why this policy applies to the application.

details.description: Evaluator-specific extra detail (e.g. what field was missing).

403.description: Caller is not an admin and does not belong to this application's company.

404.description: No application with this ID exists.

get.summary: List selectable tag/folder values from a connected security tool
get.description: Looks up the company's (or, if absent, the enterprise's) stored API credentials for the given provider and queries that vendor's API for the tag/label values a caller could use to scope this application's findings. For Wiz, the company must already be linked to a Wiz folder (via the company-level integration settings) before per-application tags can be listed. Typically called to populate a picker before calling the link endpoint below.

200.description: Available tag values for the provider.

uuid.description: Stable tag identifier (for Wiz, the raw tag string itself).

400.description: Provider not supported, no integration credentials configured for this provider, or (Wiz) the company has no folder linked yet.

403.description: Caller cannot access this application, or the vendor API rejected the stored credentials.

404.description: No application with this ID exists.

502.description: The vendor API returned an unexpected error.

503.description: Server-side integration credential encryption is not configured.

put.summary: Link an application to a tag/folder in a security tool
put.description: Creates or updates the tag-based filter that scopes which vendor findings belong to this application. The body must include `tagValue`, and that value must be one of the tags returned for the company's already-linked Wiz folder — the folder itself cannot be overridden per application. Requires the provider's integration credentials to already be configured at the company or enterprise level.

schema.description: tagValue is required; must be a tag returned by the tags endpoint for the company's linked folder.

tagValue.description: Required; must be a tag returned by the tags endpoint for the company's linked folder.

folderName.description: Informational; the folder ID itself is inherited from the company-level Wiz link.

400.description: Provider not supported, no integration credentials configured, missing required filter field, Wiz company folder not linked, or the Wiz tag is not part of the company's linked folder.

403.description: Caller cannot access this application.

404.description: No application with this ID exists.

get.summary: Get API schema metadata
get.description: Returns metadata about the application's uploaded OpenAPI/Swagger schema (filename, content type, format, size, SHA-256 checksum, uploader, and timestamps) without the raw schema text. `schema` is null if nothing has been uploaded yet.

200.description: API schema summary, or null if none uploaded.

403.description: Caller cannot access this application.

404.description: No application with this ID exists.

put.summary: Upload or replace the API schema
put.description: Uploads (or replaces the existing) OpenAPI/Swagger schema by pasting its raw text. Content must parse as JSON or YAML, be OpenAPI 3.x or Swagger 2.0, and include `info` and `paths` objects; it is capped at 2 MB and rejected if it contains binary/control characters. The server infers format from the filename extension or content shape and computes size and a SHA-256 checksum. There is exactly one API schema per application — a second call fully replaces the first.

content.description: Raw OpenAPI/Swagger document text (JSON or YAML).

filename.description: Must end in .json, .yaml, or .yml if provided; defaults to openapi.json/openapi.yaml.

400.description: Content missing/empty, disallowed filename extension, over 2 MB, contains binary data, fails to parse, or is not a valid OpenAPI 3.x / Swagger 2.0 document.

403.description: Caller cannot access this application.

404.description: No application with this ID exists.

delete.description: Deletes the application's uploaded OpenAPI/Swagger schema, if any. Idempotent: returns 204 whether or not a schema previously existed.

403.description: Caller cannot access this application.

404.description: No application with this ID exists.

get.summary: Download the raw API schema file
get.description: Streams back the raw, previously-uploaded OpenAPI/Swagger document as a file attachment (`Content-Disposition: attachment`), named `<application-name-slug>-api-schema.json` or `.yaml` based on the stored format, with the schema's original content type. Returns 404 if no schema has been uploaded for this application.

schema.description: Present when the stored format is json.
Present when the stored format is yaml.
Fallback when no more specific content type was stored.

403.description: Caller cannot access this application.

404.description: No application with this ID exists, or the application has no API schema uploaded.

get.summary: Get a structured visualization of the API schema
get.description: Parses the application's stored OpenAPI/Swagger schema and returns every endpoint (method, path, summary/description, tags), whether it requires auth and via which security scheme(s), any request/response fields matching configured sensitive-data patterns (e.g. PII, secrets), and sample request/response payloads derived from schema examples or types. Intended to let an integrator review an application's attack surface and sensitive-data exposure without implementing its own OpenAPI parser.

200.description: Visualization of the schema's endpoints and sensitive fields.

request.description: Example or type-derived sample request body.

body.description: Example or type-derived sample response body.

400.description: No schema exists to visualize is reported as 404; a stored schema that fails to re-parse or re-validate is reported here.

403.description: Caller cannot access this application.

404.description: No application with this ID exists, or it has no API schema uploaded.

get.summary: Get threat-model reference data

get.summary: Get an application's threat model

Returns `{"model": null}` if a threat model has not been started for this application yet.

put.summary: Create or update the root threat model

Checking a data type or actor that implies a sensitive surface (e.g. payment data, privileged/admin users) automatically creates a matching component node if one doesn't already exist yet, so that surface can't be left unmodeled.

403.description: Caller cannot access this application.

post.description: Creates multiple applications for a single company in one request. Every entry in `applications` must have a non-empty `name`, or the whole request is rejected with a 400 identifying the offending row. For each application, hosting domains may be supplied as a single comma/semicolon/newline-separated string via `hostingDomains` (or `domains`); each domain is cleaned (scheme and `www.` stripped), validated, normalized, and associated with the created application, creating the domain record in the company if needed. post.description: Splits one application into two: the existing application is renamed to `originalName` (defaults to its current name) and a second application named `newName` is created in the same company with the same `status`. `metadataMode` controls how much of the original's metadata the new application starts with — `all` copies every copyable field, `none` creates a blank record, and `selected` copies only the fields listed in `fields`. Only scalar metadata is ever copied: domains, deployments, deployment tokens, product links, interfaces, contacts, notes, the threat model and the API schema all stay with the original application. Both applications get a new entry in their version history (`changeSource` is `"api"` for API-key callers, `"web_form"` for session callers) and a note recording the split.

parent.description: The apex-domain record in the same company, when this domain is a subdomain and the apex is also tracked. Null for apex domains or when the apex record does not exist.

children.description: Non-empty only when this domain is itself the apex: other domains in the company sharing this apex.

siblings.description: Non-empty only when this domain is a subdomain: other subdomains in the company sharing the same apex (excluding this domain and the apex itself).

401.description: No valid session cookie or api-key header was present.

403.description: Caller is not an admin and is not a member of the domain's company.

500.description: Unexpected server error while fetching the domain.

put.description: Update a domain's `name`, `description`, `owner`, and/or `status`; only fields explicitly present in the request body are changed. A new `name` is re-validated for format, normalized, re-checked for a duplicate within the same company (excluding this domain), and its apex domain is recomputed. If the domain already has a DNS snapshot, its `metadataScore` and `totalSecurityScore` (and stored `scoreBreakdown`) are recomputed from the updated metadata without re-running any DNS lookups. This route additionally requires admin privileges.

name.description: New domain name, e.g. example.com. Re-validated and normalized to lowercase if provided.

description.description: Trimmed; empty string is stored as null.

owner.description: Trimmed; empty string is stored as null.

status.description: Defaults to "unknown" when set to an empty/blank string.

400.description: Invalid domain format, missing name (when name is provided as empty), non-string description/owner/status, or the new name conflicts with an existing domain in the same company (also returned on a Prisma unique-constraint race, code P2002).

401.description: No valid session cookie or api-key header was present.

403.description: Caller is authenticated but is not an admin.

500.description: Unexpected server error while updating the domain.

post.summary: Run a manual DNS security check (admin only)
post.description: Run a live DNS lookup against the domain's hostname (A/AAAA/CNAME/TXT/MX/NS/CAA records, DNSSEC DS records, the `_dmarc` TXT record, and TXT probes against common DKIM selectors), persisting the results as a new `DomainDnsSnapshot`. Computes a metadata-completeness score plus a DNS security score (SPF/DMARC/DKIM presence, MX+SPF+DMARC hygiene, CAA, DNSSEC, penalized for risky SPF patterns like `+all`), then diffs the new snapshot's record fields against the domain's previous snapshot and inserts one `DomainDnsChange` row per record type that was added, removed, or changed. This route additionally requires admin privileges.

201.description: DNS check completed and a new snapshot was recorded.

snapshot.description: The newly created DomainDnsSnapshot. status is ok/warning/error; error holds a semicolon-joined list of non-fatal DNS lookup issues; cnameRecords/aRecords/aaaaRecords/txtRecords/mxRecords/nsRecords/dkimRecords/scoreBreakdown are JSON-encoded strings.

changesDetected.description: Number of DomainDnsChange rows created for this check.

401.description: No valid session cookie or api-key header was present.

403.description: Caller is not an admin, or is an admin but not a member of the domain's company (getDomainForUser access check runs after requireAdmin).

500.description: Unexpected server error while running the DNS check.

get.summary: List DNS check history for a domain
get.description: Return up to the 50 most recent `DomainDnsSnapshot` rows for the domain, newest first, after verifying the caller is an admin or a member of the domain's company. A snapshot whose status is `warning` solely because of a benign DNSSEC/DS resolver rrtype error is normalized to `status: ok` with `error` cleared before being returned.

401.description: No valid session cookie or api-key header was present.

403.description: Caller is not an admin and is not a member of the domain's company.

500.description: Unexpected server error while fetching DNS snapshots.

get.summary: List detected DNS record changes for a domain
get.description: Return up to the 100 most recent `DomainDnsChange` rows for the domain, newest first, after verifying the caller is an admin or a member of the domain's company. Each row was generated by a prior `check-dns` run detecting that a record type (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, TXT/SPF/DMARC, or DKIM) was added, removed, or changed relative to the previous snapshot; severity is `warning` for A/AAAA/CNAME/MX/NS/DMARC/DKIM and `info` otherwise.

recordType.description: A, AAAA, CNAME, TXT, MX, NS, SPF, DMARC, or DKIM.

401.description: No valid session cookie or api-key header was present.

403.description: Caller is not an admin and is not a member of the domain's company.

500.description: Unexpected server error while fetching DNS changes.

post.summary: Capture a website screenshot for a domain (admin only)
post.description: Capture a full-page screenshot of the domain's website with headless Puppeteer, first asserting the domain resolves to a public (non-private/loopback) IP address, then trying `https://` and falling back to `http://` if the HTTPS attempt fails. The outcome (final URL, HTTP status, page title, load time in ms, screenshot path, or a human-readable failure reason) is stored as a `DomainWebSnapshot`; older snapshots beyond the 5 most recent for the domain are then deleted along with their screenshot files. The response includes an absolute `screenshotUrl` built from the request's host/protocol. This route additionally requires admin privileges.

201.description: Web snapshot attempt recorded (a stored snapshot with error set indicates a handled failure such as DNS not resolving, connection refused, or timeout, rather than a rejected request).

urlAttempted.description: The https:// URL that was attempted (recorded even when the http:// fallback was ultimately used).

error.description: Human-readable failure reason when the capture failed.

screenshotUrl.description: Computed absolute URL for screenshotPath, built from the request's host/protocol. Null when screenshotPath is null.

400.description: Snapshot was blocked because the domain resolves to a private/loopback network, or the domain did not resolve at all.

401.description: No valid session cookie or api-key header was present.

403.description: Caller is not an admin, or is an admin but not a member of the domain's company (getDomainForUser access check runs after requireAdmin).

500.description: Unexpected server error while running the web snapshot (e.g. the Puppeteer/Chrome runtime is unavailable on this server).

get.summary: List website screenshot history for a domain
get.description: Return the 5 most recent `DomainWebSnapshot` rows for the domain, newest first, after verifying the caller is an admin or a member of the domain's company. Each snapshot is annotated with an absolute `screenshotUrl` derived from `screenshotPath` and the current request's host/protocol (null when no screenshot was captured).

401.description: No valid session cookie or api-key header was present.

403.description: Caller is not an admin and is not a member of the domain's company.

500.description: Unexpected server error while fetching web snapshots.

put.summary: Save (create or update) an integration credential
put.description: Encrypts and stores an access key/secret pair for a vulnerability-scanner provider (WIZ), either at ENTERPRISE scope (admin only) or COMPANY scope (admin or a member of that company). accessKey/secretKey map to the OAuth client ID/secret and a tenant GraphQL baseUrl is required; the URL is normalized and stored alongside a masked hint of the access key. Upserts on (provider, scope, companyId).

companyId.description: Required when scope=COMPANY; must be omitted for ENTERPRISE.

baseUrl.description: Required tenant GraphQL endpoint for WIZ (e.g. https://api.<tenant>.app.wiz.io/graphql); optional API base for other providers.

400.description: Missing/invalid scope, companyId, accessKey/secretKey, or Wiz GraphQL URL.

403.description: Caller cannot manage this credential (not admin / not a member of companyId).

503.description: Integration encryption key not configured on the server.

get.summary: Get configuration status of an integration credential
get.description: Returns whether a credential exists for the given provider at the requested scope, without ever returning the decrypted secret. Only a masked accessKeyHint, the stored baseUrl, and updatedAt are exposed when configured.

400.description: Missing/invalid scope or companyId.

403.description: Caller cannot view this credential.

delete.description: Permanently removes the stored (encrypted) credential for a provider at the given scope. Requires the same admin/company-membership permission as saving the credential.

400.description: Missing/invalid scope or companyId.

403.description: Caller cannot delete this credential.

404.description: No credential exists for that provider/scope.

get.summary: List supported vulnerability-scanner provider ids
get.description: Returns the static list of provider identifiers supported for integration-credential CRUD and tag/folder discovery (currently WIZ). Used by the UI to populate provider pickers.

get.summary: List a provider's tags/folders available to a company
get.description: Resolves the credential that applies to this company (company-scoped, falling back to enterprise-scoped) and calls the live vendor API to list assignable groupings: Wiz folders (normalized into a tag-like shape with folder id as uuid and folder name as value/display_label). Used to populate the picker for the company's integration-link filter.

400.description: No integration credential configured for this company/provider, or unsupported provider.

403.description: Caller cannot access this company, or the vendor API denied the request with the stored credential.

503.description: Integration encryption key not configured on the server.

put.summary: Set a company's tag/folder filter for a provider
put.description: Persists the folder (Wiz) that scopes which vendor findings belong to this company. The selected folder is re-verified against the live Wiz API immediately before saving, so a stale or cross-tenant folder id cannot be persisted as a valid company boundary. Upserts CompanyToolLink on (companyId, provider).

400.description: No credential configured, invalid filter shape, or (Wiz) the selected folder was not found via the current credentials.

403.description: Caller cannot access or set a link for this company.

get.summary: Get the caller's source-control connections and connectable providers
get.description: Returns every SCM account the caller has connected (GitHub/Bitbucket/Azure DevOps today), plus which providers are configured server-side and available to connect. Includes back-compat convenience fields (connected/login/avatarUrl) mirroring the first connection for older clients expecting a single-connection model.

get.summary: Start an SCM OAuth connect flow
get.description: Begins the OAuth/app-install flow for the given provider (defaults to GITHUB): generates a random state, stashes it in the session alongside the provider/host, and returns the vendor authorize URL to redirect the browser to. The provider must be configured server-side (client id/secret set) or a 503 is returned. Completion happens out-of-band at GET /api/integrations/scm/callback, which is not a client-invoked API operation.

302.description: Redirect to the provider's OAuth authorize URL (state persisted in session for the callback to validate).

400.description: Unsupported provider.

500.description: Failed to persist connect state / start the flow.

503.description: Provider is not configured server-side (missing client id/secret).

delete.summary: Disconnect one or all of the caller's SCM connections
delete.description: Deletes the SCM connection with the given id (if it belongs to the caller), or all of the caller's connections when no id is supplied.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Connection id to disconnect; omit to disconnect all of the caller's connections.

get.summary: List repositories across all of the caller's SCM connections
get.description: Fans out to every connected SCM account and lists the repositories visible to each (owner/name, URL, default branch, privacy, description). A per-connection failure is logged and yields an empty list for that connection rather than failing the whole request.

400.description: Caller has no SCM connections.

get.summary: Preview a repository's detected language/framework without linking it
get.description: Fetches live metadata plus detected top languages and manifest-derived dependencies/frameworks for a given owner/name repository, used to prefill the New Application form before any link is persisted. Does not write to the database.

parameters.name: connectionId
parameters.description: Which of the caller's connections to use; defaults to their oldest connection when omitted.

400.description: Missing owner/name, or no SCM connection could be resolved.

404.description: Repository not found or not accessible with the resolved connection.

502.description: SCM API error reading the repository.

get.summary: Search which applications depend on a given package
get.description: Cross-application, security-relevant lookup: finds every stored RepoDependency row matching the given package name (case-insensitive) and optional ecosystem, then reports every linked application that pulls it in. Results are filtered to applications in the caller's own company unless the caller is an admin, so non-admins cannot enumerate other companies' dependency usage.

parameters.name: ecosystem
parameters.description: e.g. npm, pypi, maven, go, rubygems, nuget, composer.

400.description: Missing required "name" query parameter.

get.summary: Get a company- or division-scoped dependency inventory (SBOM) across applications
get.description: Returns a flattened, security-relevant software bill of materials: every (dependency, application) pairing for repositories linked to in-scope applications, each row including ecosystem, package name/version, whether it's a recognized framework, and the owning application/company. Non-admins are always scoped to their own company; admins may additionally filter by companyId or divisionId, or omit both to see every company. Capped at 10000 rows (truncated flag set when the cap is hit) and includes facet lists (distinct ecosystems, distinct companies) for client-side filtering.

parameters.name: companyId
parameters.description: Admin only: scope to one company.

parameters.name: divisionId
parameters.description: Admin only: scope to one division (ignored if companyId is also set).

put.summary: Link a source-control repository to an application
put.description: Resolves owner/name either directly or by parsing a repository URL (GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket/Azure DevOps, https or ssh), fetches live repo metadata/languages/dependencies through the caller's resolved SCM connection, upserts the shared ScmRepo row, runs a best-effort OSV advisory scan over its dependencies, and points the application's repoUrl at it. Only an admin or a member of the application's company may link it.

url.description: Repository URL, used to derive owner/name when owner/name are not both provided.

connectionId.description: Which of the caller's SCM connections to use; defaults to their oldest connection.

400.description: Owner/name (or a parseable URL) not provided, or no SCM connection could be resolved.

403.description: Caller cannot access this application.

404.description: Application not found, or the repository was not found/accessible.

502.description: SCM API error reading the repository.

delete.description: Removes the ApplicationScmRepo link and clears the application's repoUrl. Previously-applied language/framework values on the application are left untouched.

403.description: Caller cannot access this application.

post.summary: Refresh an application's linked repository snapshot and dependencies
post.description: Re-fetches metadata, languages, and dependencies for the already-linked repo (using a connection matching the linked repo's provider/host), re-runs the best-effort OSV advisory scan, and re-persists the ScmRepo/RepoDependency rows. Does not change which repo is linked.

400.description: No repository linked to this application, or no matching SCM connection could be resolved.

403.description: Caller cannot access this application.

502.description: SCM API error syncing the repository.

post.summary: Re-run OSV advisory scanning against an application's already-stored dependencies
post.description: Re-queries OSV.dev for the dependencies already stored for the application's linked repo (no re-fetch from the SCM provider) and updates each RepoDependency's osvScanned/osvVulnIds/osvVulns/osvScannedAt fields, because advisory data changes over time even when code doesn't. Wiz remains the system of record for authoritative vulnerability data; this is a supplementary, best-effort signal.

summary.description: Scan summary returned by the OSV scanner (counts of scanned/flagged dependencies).

400.description: No repository linked to this application.

403.description: Caller cannot access this application.

post.summary: Apply detected (or explicit) language/framework onto an application
post.description: Writes language and/or framework onto the application's official fields. When the request body omits a field, the value detected from the linked repo's languages/dependencies is used instead; if neither an explicit value nor a detected value is available for either field, nothing is written and a 400 is returned.

language.description: Explicit override; otherwise the detected top language(s) are used.

framework.description: Explicit override; otherwise the detected framework label(s) are used.

400.description: No repository linked to this application, or nothing to apply (no explicit or detected language/framework).

403.description: Caller cannot access this application.

get.summary: List policies
get.description: Without a `forCompany` query parameter, returns the full admin list of all policies (any scope, active or inactive) with each policy's control count, ordered by `displayOrder` then `createdAt`; this branch requires admin. With `forCompany=<companyId>`, returns the reduced set of *active* policies that actually apply to that company (global policies, policies assigned to the company's division, or policies assigned directly to the company) along with a human-readable `reason` for each match; this branch is allowed for an admin or for a caller whose own `companyId` equals the requested company.

parameters.name: forCompany
parameters.description: Company ID to compute applicable policies for. When omitted, the full admin policy list is returned instead and admin access is required.

200.description: Either the full admin policy list (no `forCompany`) or the list of policies applicable to the given company (`forCompany` present).

oneOf.description: Admin view: all policies with control counts.

controls.description: Number of controls belonging to this policy.

reason.description: Why this policy applies, e.g. "Applies to all", "Assigned to this company", "Assigned to <Division> division".

403.description: Not an admin and either no `forCompany` was given, or `forCompany` does not match the caller's own company.

post.description: Creates a new policy. `scope` must be one of `global`, `division`, `company`, or `conditional`. Division-scoped policies require a non-empty `divisionIds` array (all must exist), company-scoped policies require a non-empty `companyIds` array (all must exist), and conditional-scoped policies require `targetingRules`. `targetingRules` (a JSON object or JSON-encoded string, e.g. `{ "type": "conditional", "conditions": [...] }`) is stored as a JSON string; for `global` scope it defaults to `{ "type": "global" }` when not supplied. The created policy is returned together with its division/company assignments.

targetingRules.description: JSON object (or JSON-encoded string) describing targeting, e.g. `{ "type": "conditional", "conditions": [...] }`. Required when `scope` is `conditional`; defaulted to `{ "type": "global" }` when `scope` is `global` and omitted.

divisionIds.description: Division IDs this policy applies to. Required (non-empty) when `scope` is `division`.

companyIds.description: Company IDs this policy applies to. Required (non-empty) when `scope` is `company`.

400.description: Validation error: missing/invalid `name`, invalid `scope`, missing `divisionIds`/`companyIds`/`targetingRules` for the given scope, invalid targeting rules JSON/type, or a referenced division/company ID that does not exist.

get.summary: Get a policy by ID
get.description: For an admin caller, returns the full policy record including every control (with its fields) and the raw division/company assignment lists. For a non-admin caller with a company context, returns a reduced, read-only projection (no targeting/assignment lists; `isActive` controls/fields only) and only if this policy actually applies to the caller's company, as determined the same way as `GET /api/policies?forCompany=`.

200.description: Policy details. Admins receive the full record; company members receive a read-only subset with `readOnly: true`.

403.description: No company context for a non-admin caller, or this policy does not apply to the caller's company.

put.description: Partially updates a policy; only provided fields are changed. If `scope` becomes (or already is) `division`/`company` and `divisionIds`/`companyIds` is supplied, it must be a non-empty array of existing IDs and fully replaces the policy's existing division/company assignments (the other assignment type's rows are left alone unless its own ID list is also supplied). `targetingRules` may be set to `null` to clear it, an object/JSON string to replace it, or omitted to leave it unchanged.

200.description: Updated policy with its division/company assignments (same shape as the create response).

400.description: Validation error: invalid `scope`, invalid targeting rules JSON/type, empty `divisionIds`/`companyIds` for the applicable scope, or a referenced division/company ID that does not exist.

delete.description: Deletes a policy, but only if it currently has zero controls; a policy with one or more controls must have those controls removed or reassigned first. On success the database cascade also removes the policy's division/company assignment rows.

400.description: Policy still has controls attached.

message.example: This policy has 3 control(s). Please remove or reassign all controls before deleting.

patch.description: Sets a policy's `displayOrder`, which controls its sort position in policy listings (lower values first). Only `displayOrder` is accepted; it must be present and numeric.

400.description: `displayOrder` missing or not a number.

error.example: displayOrder is required and must be a number

500.description: Failed to update policy order (also returned if the policy ID does not exist, since that case is not distinguished from other errors).

get.summary: List policy controls
get.description: Returns policy controls (each including its field checks and a summary of the parent policy), ordered by `displayOrder`. Pass `policyId` to restrict the list to controls belonging to one policy.

parameters.name: policyId
parameters.description: Restrict results to controls belonging to this policy.

200.description: Array of policy controls with fields and parent policy summary.

post.description: Creates a control under an existing policy (`policyId` is required and must reference a real policy). `controlId` must be a globally unique code (e.g. "3.4.2"). `evaluationLogic` (`AND` or `OR`, default `AND`) says how the control's `fields` are combined when evaluating an application. Each entry in `fields` becomes a `PolicyControlField` row: `fieldPath` names the application attribute to check, `operator` is the comparison, and `value` (any JSON-serializable value) is stored JSON-encoded.

policyId.description: ID of the policy this control belongs to.

400.description: Validation error: missing `controlId`/`name`/`description`/`policyId`, `policyId` does not reference an existing policy, invalid `evaluationLogic`, or `controlId` already in use.

get.summary: Get a policy control by ID
get.description: Returns a single control including its field checks and the parent policy's `id`/`name`/`scope`.

200.description: Policy control with fields and parent policy summary.

put.description: Partially updates a control; only provided fields are changed (falsy/empty-string values for `controlId`, `name`, or `description` are rejected rather than clearing them). If `policyId` is supplied it must reference an existing policy, moving the control to that policy. If `fields` is supplied, it fully replaces the control's existing field checks (all existing `PolicyControlField` rows are deleted and the new array is inserted).

200.description: Updated control with fields and parent policy summary.

400.description: Validation error: empty `controlId`/`name`/`description`, `policyId` does not reference an existing policy, invalid `evaluationLogic`, or `controlId` collides with another control.

delete.description: Deletes a control. Its `PolicyControlField` rows are removed via cascade. Note the schema also has `PolicyControlOverride` rows (manual per-application compliance overrides) that reference the control with cascading delete, so deleting a control also removes any manual overrides recorded against it.

patch.summary: Update a policy control's display order
patch.description: Sets a control's `displayOrder`, which controls its sort position within its policy (lower values first). Only `displayOrder` is accepted; it must be present and numeric.

200.description: Control with its updated `displayOrder` (base fields only, no `fields`/`policy` include).

400.description: `displayOrder` missing or not a number.

error.example: Display order is required and must be a number

get.summary: List products
get.description: Returns products scoped to the caller's company. Admins see all companies by default, or can narrow the result with `companyId`/`divisionId` query parameters (an admin-only convenience scope; it can never widen a non-admin caller's access). Each product includes its owning company and a count of mapped applications.

parameters.description: Admin-only. Restrict results to companies belonging to this division.

post.description: Creates a new product under a company. Fails with 400 if a product with the same name already exists for the company.

get.description: Returns the component types (e.g. Frontend, Backend API, Data Store) available for classifying applications mapped to a product within a company. On first access for a company, a default set of component types is seeded automatically. Admins may pass companyId to view another company's types; non-admins are restricted to their own company.

parameters.name: companyId
parameters.description: Company to list component types for. Defaults to the caller's company. Admin-only to specify a different company.

500.description: Failed to fetch product component types.

post.description: Creates a custom component type for a company, used to classify applications when mapping them to a product. Non-admins may only create types for their own company. Fails with 400 if a type with the same name already exists for the company.

400.description: Missing name, missing companyId, or duplicate name for company.

403.description: Non-admin caller attempted to create a type for another company.

500.description: Failed to create product component type.

get.summary: Calculate and record a product's score
get.description: Computes an aggregate security score for a product by averaging the AppSec knowledge/tool/total scores of its mapped applications, and the average policy compliance percentage across those applications. If no applications are mapped, a zeroed score is recorded. Every call persists a new ProductScore history record (for score-over-time tracking) and returns the freshly calculated values.

403.description: Caller is not in the same company as the product.

get.summary: Get a product
get.description: Returns a single product with its full architecture: mapped applications (each with its component type), data flows between mapped applications, and ingress points. This is the data used to render a product's architecture/threat-model diagram. Restricted to callers in the product's company, or admins.

200.description: Product with applications, data flows, and ingress points.

put.description: Updates a product's editable fields. Only fields present in the request body are changed. If name is provided it cannot be empty, and businessCriticality (if provided and non-null) must be an integer between 1 and 5. Restricted to callers in the product's company, or admins.

400.description: Empty name, invalid businessCriticality, or duplicate name for company.

403.description: Caller is not in the same company as the product.

delete.description: Permanently deletes a product and, via cascading relations, its application mappings, data flows, ingress points, and score history. Admin only.

403.description: Caller is authenticated but not an admin.

post.summary: Map an application to a product

Optionally, in the same transaction, this can also create a data flow from an already-mapped connectFromApplicationId into the new application, and/or mark the new application as an ingress point (markAsIngress with an optional ingressChannel and requiresApiKey).

404.description: Product, application, or component type not found.

500.description: Failed to add application to product.

put.description: Updates the component classification (componentTypeId or customComponentLabel) and/or displayOrder for an application already mapped to a product. At least one of componentTypeId or customComponentLabel must resolve to a non-empty value after the update.

delete.summary: Unmap an application from a product

403.description: Caller is not in the same company as the product.

404.description: Product not found, or mapping not found.

500.description: Failed to remove application from product.

get.summary: List a product's ingress points
get.description: Returns the points where external traffic is considered to enter the product's architecture — each tied to a mapped application and a named channel (e.g. "default", a specific API path). Used alongside data flows to render the product's threat-model diagram.

500.description: Failed to fetch product ingress points.

post.summary: Add an ingress point to a product
post.description: Marks a mapped application as an entry point for external traffic into the product's architecture, on a named channel (upserted on productId+applicationId+channel, so calling again with the same channel updates requiresApiKey instead of duplicating). The application must already be mapped to the product.

403.description: Caller is not in the same company as the product.

500.description: Failed to create product ingress point.

delete.summary: Remove an ingress point from a product
delete.description: Deletes a single ingress point belonging to the given product.

403.description: Caller is not in the same company as the product.

404.description: Product not found, or ingress point not found on this product.

get.summary: List a product's data flows
get.description: Returns the data flows recorded between applications mapped to a product — each flow describes a directed connection (source to target, with protocol, data classification, and whether it requires an API key). Together with ingress points, these form the edges of the product's architecture/threat-model diagram.

403.description: Caller is not in the same company as the product.

500.description: Failed to fetch product data flows.

post.summary: Create a data flow for a product
post.description: Records a directed data flow between two applications mapped to the product, for use in the product's architecture/threat-model diagram. Both sourceApplicationId and targetApplicationId must differ, belong to the same company as the product, and already be mapped to the product.

400.description: Missing/equal application IDs, applications not in the same company, or not mapped to this product.

403.description: Caller is not in the same company as the product.

404.description: Product not found, or source/target application does not exist.

500.description: Failed to create product data flow.

put.description: Updates fields of an existing data flow. If sourceApplicationId or targetApplicationId is changed, the same validation as creation is re-run (different applications, same company, both mapped to the product).

400.description: Invalid source/target application combination on re-validation.

403.description: Caller is not in the same company as the product.

404.description: Product not found, or data flow not found on this product.

500.description: Failed to update product data flow.

delete.description: Deletes a single data flow belonging to the given product.

403.description: Caller is not in the same company as the product.

404.description: Product not found, or data flow not found on this product.

500.description: Failed to delete product data flow.

get.summary: List published product updates
get.description: Returns platform changelog entries that are published (status "published" with a publishedAt timestamp), newest first, for display to any signed-in user. This is the general-audience feed; draft/unpublished updates are never returned here. Supports an optional limit (default 50, capped between 1 and 100).

get.summary: Get the active OWASP SAMM framework definition
get.description: Returns the active OWASP SAMM v2.0 framework (created on first request via ensureSammFramework if it does not yet exist), including its 5 business-function domains and the 15 practices nested beneath them, each enriched with its Atlas SAMM-aligned question bank. Available to any authenticated user; the response is not scoped to a company since the framework itself is shared across all companies.

200.description: The active SAMM framework, its domains/practices, and scoring guidance.

practices.description: Flattened list of all 15 practices across all domains, each with its two Atlas SAMM questions.

scoring.example: Each practice score is the average of its two Atlas SAMM-aligned question responses.

401.description: Not authenticated (no valid session cookie or api-key).

500.description: Failed to fetch or lazily create the SAMM framework.

get.summary: List SAMM assessments
get.description: Lists SAMM assessments, most recently created first, including their nested framework/domains/practices, company, creator, reviewer, and a computed completion summary. Non-admin callers are always scoped to their own company (the `companyId` query parameter is ignored for them); admins may optionally pass `companyId` to filter, and if they omit it the endpoint returns assessments across every company.

parameters.name: companyId
parameters.description: Restrict results to this company. Only honored for admin callers; non-admin callers are always restricted to their own company regardless of this value.

200.description: Array of SAMM assessments with a computed `summary` field.

403.description: Non-admin caller has no company context to scope the listing to.

post.description: Starts a new draft SAMM assessment for a company, attached to the currently active framework. Admins may target any company via `companyId` in the body; non-admin callers may only create an assessment for their own company. Returns 404 if the resolved company does not exist and 403 if the caller lacks access to it.

companyId.description: Company to create the assessment for. Admin-only; ignored (the caller's own company is used) for non-admin callers.

ownerName.description: Free-text name of the person who owns/drives this assessment.

403.description: No resolvable company, or caller does not have access to the target company.

get.summary: Get a single SAMM assessment
get.description: Fetches one SAMM assessment by ID with its full framework/domains/practices, company, creator, reviewer, and recorded responses, plus a computed `summary` (assessed practice count, average score, completion percentage). Access is limited to admins or users belonging to the assessment's company.

framework.description: Full nested framework/domains/practices, as returned by GET /api/samm/framework.

averageScore.description: Only populated once every practice has a score.

403.description: Caller is neither an admin nor a member of this assessment's company.

put.summary: Save or submit responses on a draft SAMM assessment
put.description: Upserts per-practice responses (answers, rationale, evidence reference) on a draft assessment and recomputes each practice's score from its two Atlas SAMM question answers. Only assessments in `draft` status may be edited (409 if already completed/archived). Setting `status: "completed"` submits the assessment, which requires a scored response for all 15 practices and sets `submittedAt` plus a `nextDueAt` six months out; otherwise the assessment remains a draft.

responses.description: One entry per practice being answered; each practice may appear at most once and must belong to this assessment's framework.

answers.description: Answers keyed by question ID, e.g. {"q1": 2, "q2": 3}.

status.description: Pass "completed" to submit the assessment; any other value (or omission) keeps it in draft.

400.description: A response referenced an unknown or duplicate practice, `answers` was not an object keyed by stream/question ID, or `status: "completed"` was submitted without a valid score for all 15 practices.

403.description: Caller is neither an admin nor a member of this assessment's company.

409.description: Assessment is not in `draft` status and can no longer be edited.

get.summary: List all notes for a company
get.description: Returns every note visible for a company: company-level notes plus every note attached to any application belonging to that company, merged and sorted newest-first. Application notes additionally embed the `application` they belong to. Returns 404 if the company does not exist.

200.description: Combined list of company and application notes for this company, newest first.

applicationId.description: Set for application notes; null for company-level notes.

403.description: Caller is authenticated but not an admin.

post.description: Creates a note attached directly to a company (not to any application). Requires a non-empty `content` string of at most 5000 characters and that the target company exists.

content.description: Note text, must be non-empty after trimming.

400.description: `content` missing/empty or longer than 5000 characters.

403.description: Caller is authenticated but not an admin.

get.summary: List all notes for an application
get.description: Returns every note attached to a single application, newest first, each with its creating user. Returns 404 if the application does not exist.

200.description: List of notes for this application, newest first.

403.description: Caller is authenticated but not an admin.

post.description: Creates a note attached to a specific application. Requires a non-empty `content` string of at most 5000 characters and that the target application exists.

content.description: Note text, must be non-empty after trimming.

400.description: `content` missing/empty or longer than 5000 characters.

403.description: Caller is authenticated but not an admin.

put.description: Replaces the text content of an existing note (company or application note). Requires a non-empty `content` string of at most 5000 characters and that the note exists.

content.description: New note text, must be non-empty after trimming.

400.description: `content` missing/empty or longer than 5000 characters.

403.description: Caller is authenticated but not an admin.

delete.description: Permanently deletes a note (company or application) by ID. Returns 404 if no note with that ID exists.

403.description: Caller is authenticated but not an admin.
